summary: Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A doctoral student at Peking University, he studied under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Bai Su, and Shichang Ma, and was affiliated with Peking University in 2017.

Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1921–1924) and under scholars including Hakuju Ui, Sylvain Lévi, and Taiken Kimura, later serving on Tokyo's staff (1926) and as professor at Toyo University (1927).

Glenn H. Mullin (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous traditional masters, including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (circa 1902–1917).
Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, he held posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi.

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at University Maharani College and University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis and others, he served as librarian at Sarasvati Bhavan Library (1914–1920) and Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1923–1937).

Gordon Dester Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University, held posts at Pomona College and Vanderbilt University, and served as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University from 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (circa 1908–1911) and served as a professor at the University of Yangon from circa 1912 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson (born 1943) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, he served as Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge (1974–2010), President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (circa 1810–1815) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (circa 1823–1844).

Gottfried August Bürger (1747–1794) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1768 to 1772 and later held a post there from circa 1784 to 1794.

Gottfried Bernhardy (1800–1875) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1817–1820) and held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck (1762–1824) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (circa 1782–1786) and held a post at Vilnius University from circa 1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena, later serving at Leipzig University as an extraordinary professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

Gottfried Kinkel (1815–1882) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn (circa 1831–1834), where he also held a post from circa 1837 to 1848, before holding a post at ETH Zurich (circa 1866–1882).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at King's College London and Heidelberg, he served as Principal of Government College University, Lahore (1864), and first Registrar of the University of the Punjab (circa 1882–1885).

Gouriswar Bhattacharya (1924–2013) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin, serving there from circa 1974 to 2005, including as Lehrbeauftragter from circa 1975 to 2005.

Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya, held professorships and Vice-Chancellorships at the Universities of Allahabad and Rajasthan, and chaired the Allahabad Museum and Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) was an Indologist and sociologist. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon, subsequently serving as Head of the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai from 1924 to 1959.
